title: Equality of split search outputs
statement: For a function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and a Boolean word $w$, splitting $w$ at the length of the first accepted iterate of the split step and encoding the two pieces gives the same word as splitting at the index returned by the least-index search for $i+f(i)=|w|$. If that search returns none, both expressions give the empty word.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a function from natural numbers to natural numbers
replaced:
Splitting $w$ at the length of the first orbit candidate accepted by the
width-parametric test and pair encoding the two halves gives the same word
as splitting $w$ at the index returned by the width-parametric split search
for $f$; when both searches fail, both sides are the empty word.
